title: Security architecture: containerized agent with tool gateway
description:
The agent runs in a Docker container with NO secrets, NO network egress, and minimal mounts (one RW /workspace). The ONLY way out is a Unix domain socket to a Tool Gateway on the host.

The gateway holds: SecretsManager (in-memory decrypted creds), service proxies (LiteLLM, Discord, Telegram), approval UI/CLI, and an audit log.

This is the foundational security model for everything else — REPL sandbox, sub-agent shards, module system. Nothing else ships until this boundary exists.

Key properties:
- "print process.env" is irrelevant — no secrets in container at all
- No direct internet access — can't exfiltrate via fetch/curl
- Mounts are the filesystem boundary — /workspace RW only
- Approval gating: gateway issues short-lived scoped capability tokens after human approval for anything outside the play area
- isolated-vm becomes guardrails inside the container, not the wall
design:
Architecture:

[Agent container: no secrets, no egress, minimal mounts]
   |  unix domain socket (mounted file)
   v
[Tool Gateway (host)]
   |-- SecretsManager (SOPS+age → in-memory Map)
   |-- LiteLLM proxy (LLM keys)
   |-- Discord narrow API (sendMessage, readChannel — NOT raw HTTP proxy)
   |-- File broker (reads/writes outside /workspace need approval)
   |-- Net broker (POST/PUT to non-allowlisted destinations need approval)
   |-- Approval UI/CLI (human in the loop)
   '-- Audit log (every request logged)

Gateway policy per request: ALLOW / DENY / NEEDS_APPROVAL
- fs.read/write under /workspace → ALLOW
- fs.read/write outside /workspace → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- net.* with request body or non-allowlisted dest → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- discord.sendMessage → ALLOW (within configured channels)
- llm.complete → ALLOW (within budget)

Capability tokens:
- scope = (method, domain/path OR filesystem prefix)
- constraints = (max bytes, TTL, optional one-time use)
- Agent cannot forge — issued by gateway after approval

Container setup:
- docker run --network=none
- Mount: /workspace (RW), /run/gateway.sock (RO)
- No env vars with secrets
- No /home, /etc, /run/secrets mounts

Phases:
1. Container + gateway skeleton (no egress, socket comm, fs.read/write for /workspace)
2. LiteLLM integration behind gateway
3. Discord narrow API behind gateway
4. Approval UI/CLI + capability tokens
5. Audit logging
6. isolated-vm as inner guardrails
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent container has --network=none and no secrets in env/mounts
- Agent can ONLY communicate via Unix socket to gateway
- fs operations outside /workspace are blocked or require approval
- LLM calls route through gateway → LiteLLM, agent never sees API keys
- Discord calls go through narrow typed API, not raw HTTP proxy
- All gateway requests are audit logged
- Approval flow works for privileged operations
notes:
Sprint 4 complete. Core security architecture implemented:

Done:
- Phase 1: Container + gateway skeleton (JSON-RPC 2.0 over NDJSON Unix socket)
- Phase 3: Discord narrow typed API (discord.send, discord.typing, discord.message notification)
- Phase 4 partial: CLI approval flow for privileged ops (y/N prompt)
- Phase 5: Persistent SQLite audit logging (every RPC call with timing + errors)
- Policy engine: workspace ALLOW, outside NEEDS_APPROVAL, unknown DENY
- Content sanitization: 3-layer pipeline (pattern detection → HTML strip → untrusted tagging)
- Docker: Dockerfile.agent + docker-compose.yml with --network=none
- 30 new tests (policy, sanitization, audit)

Remaining (Phase 2 enhancements, not blocking):
- LiteLLM integration (tracked as PSFN-cf3)
- Capability tokens with TTL + scoping
- isolated-vm inner guardrails

6/7 acceptance criteria met. The missing one (LiteLLM) is child issue PSFN-cf3.
close_reason: All 7 acceptance criteria met. Gateway/agent split, Docker --network=none, policy engine, CLI approval, audit logging, content sanitization, LiteLLM proxy (PSFN-cf3), Discord narrow API. Remaining enhancements (capability tokens, isolated-vm) are future work.

title: Structured logging and debug levels
description: Replace ad-hoc console.log/console.error with structured logging that supports debug levels (error, warn, info, debug, trace). Ensure no errors are swallowed silently — all catch blocks must log. Add debug-level logging to: LLM calls (model, tokens, latency), memory extraction (what was extracted), session I/O (appends, loads), REPL sandbox execution, shard lifecycle, Discord message flow.
acceptance_criteria:
- Configurable log level via LOG_LEVEL env var (default: info)
- All catch blocks log errors
- Debug level shows LLM call details, memory operations, session I/O
- No silent error swallowing anywhere in the codebase
close_reason: Winston structured logging implemented across all 13 production files. createComponentLogger() factory, configurable LOG_LEVEL env var, component-tagged output format. Demo/CLI scripts intentionally retain console.log for interactive terminal output.

title: LiteLLM proxy for credential isolation — Purrsephone never sees real API keys
description:
Deploy LiteLLM as a local proxy (localhost:4000) between Purrsephone's runtime and upstream LLM providers. The agent process only holds a virtual key; real provider credentials (OpenRouter, Z.AI, DeepSeek, etc.) stay server-side in the proxy.

pi-ai has explicit LiteLLM support — define custom Model objects with baseUrl pointing at the proxy and compat: { supportsStore: false }.

Scope: LiteLLM config for OpenRouter wildcard + Z.AI direct + model aliases, Docker Compose deployment, virtual key with budget/rate limits, secret redaction guardrail for messages.
design:
Architecture:
  Purrsephone (Node.js) --[virtual key]--> LiteLLM (localhost:4000) --[real keys]--> OpenRouter / Z.AI / DeepSeek

Config: proxy/litellm_config.yaml with model_list (openrouter/*, zai/glm-5, deepseek-v3.2, kimi-k2.5)
Deploy: proxy/docker-compose.yml (litellm image + optional PostgreSQL for virtual keys)
Secrets: proxy/.env holds real API keys, gitignored
Integration: Custom pi-ai Model objects with baseUrl=http://localhost:4000/v1, provider='litellm'

Reference: BotMaker keyring-proxy at /mnt/samesung/ai/botmaker/proxy/ uses same zero-trust pattern (Fastify, AES-256-GCM, tag-based routing). LiteLLM is preferred over porting keyring-proxy because pi-ai already documents the integration.

Key files to create:
- proxy/litellm_config.yaml
- proxy/docker-compose.yml
- proxy/.env (gitignored)
- src/llm/models.ts (pi-ai Model definitions pointing at proxy)
close_reason: Implemented: LiteLLM proxy config (proxy/litellm_config.yaml, proxy/docker-compose.yml), pi-ai model factory (src/llm/models.ts), LLMClient integration (auto-routes through proxy when LITELLM_BASE_URL is set), 8 new tests. Works transparently in single-process, gateway, and agent modes.

title: RLM+REPL Sandbox — context-as-object, programmatic memory access, sub-LM calls, self-modification
description:
Port the RLM (Recursive Language Model) paradigm into PSFN. Core insight: context is an object Purrsephone can programmatically inspect/query/transform, not tokens stuffed into a prompt. She decides what context she needs.

Reference: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24601

**Foundation:** pi-agent-core's `Agent` class is the base layer. PSFN already depends on `@mariozechner/pi-ai`; pi-agent-core (1,495 LoC, MIT, single dep) provides the agent loop with streaming events, steering, follow-ups, and declaration-merging extensibility. Build RLM on top of this, don't reimplement.

**What RLM adds on top of pi-agent-core:**
1. REPL sandbox — persistent code execution environment (TypeScript). Model writes ```repl blocks, system executes them, returns truncated output.
2. Context-as-object — memories (SQLite L2), sessions (pi JSONL), identity, modules exposed as queryable interfaces in REPL namespace.
3. Sub-LM calls — `llm_query()` / `llm_query_batched()` in REPL, routes through LLMProvider / pi-agent-core's streamFn. Delegate to cheaper models for bulk work.
4. Modified termination — `FINAL()` / `FINAL_VAR()` signals completion.
5. Self-modification — write/test/install modules at runtime via REPL.

**Recommended approach:** Dual-mode agent loop via pi-agent-core's Agent. Conversational mode (standard pi agent loop for chat) + cognitive mode (RLM-style for complex reasoning). Mode triggered by model request, event type, or user directive.

**New files (~800 LoC per spec):**
- `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — REPL environment with restricted globals, persistent state
- `src/repl/context.ts` — Context object exposing memories, sessions, identity, modules
- `src/repl/sub-lm.ts` — llm_query/llm_query_batched routing through pi's streamFn
- Agent integration via pi-agent-core's Agent callbacks (transformContext, convertToLlm)

**Security:** Gateway/agent split with --network=none Docker already provides the security boundary.
design: Dual-mode AgentLoop: detect ```repl blocks vs standard tool calls in model output, dispatch accordingly. Preserves backward compatibility. RLM loop: prompt -> extract code blocks (regex) -> execute in sandbox -> check FINAL() -> append truncated output -> repeat. Sandbox uses node:vm or similar restricted execution. Context objects are lazy-loaded interfaces (don't materialize full DB into memory). Sub-LM calls reuse existing LLMProvider interface.
close_reason: Implemented RLM+REPL sandbox: types, parser, vm sandbox, RLM iteration loop, think tool. 476 LoC production + 503 LoC tests. All 137 tests pass, clean build.

title: Minimal Scheduler (MVP) — heartbeat, cron, one-shot, memory maintenance
description: Build the scheduler layer (~400 LoC) per spec Layer 6. Heartbeat timer (default 30min), cron/every/one-shot task registry, memory maintenance hooks. Emit schedule.tick, schedule.task.run, schedule.heartbeat events. First concrete task: Purrsephone sends a Discord heartbeat message every hour. Design collaboratively with Purrsephone via CLI chat.
design: Files: src/scheduler/types.ts, src/scheduler/scheduler.ts, src/scheduler/heartbeat.ts. Events: schedule.tick (every interval), schedule.task.run (when a task executes), schedule.heartbeat (when heartbeat fires). Task types: cron (recurring), every (interval-based), one-shot (at specific time). Heartbeat is a special every-task that triggers Purrsephone to review state and optionally act. Memory maintenance (salience decay) already exists as SalienceDecay — register it as a scheduler task. Wire into runtime.ts + index.ts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduler starts with runtime, registers built-in maintenance tasks
- Heartbeat fires at configurable interval, emits schedule.heartbeat
- Cron/every/one-shot tasks execute on schedule
- Events emitted for all task runs
- Discord heartbeat message sent hourly as proof of life
- Tests for scheduler logic (not time-dependent — use manual tick)
close_reason: Scheduler MVP implemented: types (TaskType, TaskState, ScheduledTask, SchedulerConfig), Scheduler class (register/unregister/start/stop/tick, heartbeat as special task), 17 unit tests, wired into runtime.ts (salience decay + heartbeat as scheduler tasks, Discord hourly heartbeat via DISCORD_HEARTBEAT_CHANNEL env), wired into agent-main.ts. 166 total tests passing.

title: Session layer: migrate from SQLite to pi SessionManager (JSONL trees) + native compaction
description:
**Architectural correction:** Conversations belong in pi's JSONL tree sessions, not SQLite. SQLite is for the memory system (L2 extracted memories with embeddings). JSONL sessions ARE the L0 immutable archive.

**Current state (wrong):**
- `session/store.ts` — SQLite `session_entries` table storing conversations
- `session/manager.ts` — wraps SQLite store, builds context
- `memory/store.ts` — SQLite `l0_archive` table duplicating conversation data
- `session/store.ts` — SQLite `compaction_summaries` table (reimplements what pi does natively)

**Target state:**
- Use `@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent`'s `SessionManager` for conversations (JSONL trees, branching, compaction built-in)
- Or use `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core`'s session primitives if sufficient
- Drop SQLite session_entries and compaction_summaries tables
- Drop L0 archive table (JSONL IS L0 — every message, immutable, forever)
- Keep SQLite MemoryStore for L2 memories (extracted facts, emotions, semantic — the salient parts)
- Memory extraction process reads from JSONL sessions, writes to SQLite memory store

**What we get for free from pi:**
- JSONL tree sessions with branching
- Native compaction (shouldCompact, prepareCompaction, compact — all exported)
- buildSessionContext() for context window assembly
- Session versioning and migration

**Migration path:**
1. Add pi-agent-core Agent class as the agent loop foundation (replace current AgentLoop)
2. Use pi's SessionManager for conversations
3. Wire memory extraction to read from JSONL sessions instead of SQLite
4. Remove SQLite session tables (session_entries, compaction_summaries, l0_archive)
5. Keep MemoryStore (SQLite + sqlite-vec) for L2 extracted memories only

This is really L3 context management — pi handles it natively.
design: Use pi's SessionManager (JSONL trees) for conversations. Use pi's compaction natively (shouldCompact/prepareCompaction/compact are all exported). Wire memory extraction to read from JSONL sessions. Drop SQLite session_entries, compaction_summaries, and l0_archive tables. MemoryStore (SQLite + sqlite-vec) stays for L2 extracted memories only.
close_reason: Session migration complete. SQLite → JSONL files, l0_archive removed, L0Archiver removed, 138→149 tests all pass.

title: Module system — hot-loadable TypeScript modules, self-installable via REPL
description:
Module registry + hot-loader for TypeScript modules. Purrsephone can build and install her own modules via the REPL sandbox. Modules register tools, subscribe to events, and have lifecycle hooks (init/start/stop/health).

**What exists:** Lifecycle interface in types.ts, tool registration via AgentLoop.registerTool(), event bus for composition. No module registry, no hot-loading, no jiti dependency.

**Planned files (~500 LoC per spec):**
- `src/modules/registry.ts` — module registry with install/uninstall/list
- `src/modules/loader.ts` — hot-load TypeScript via jiti (no compilation needed)
- `src/modules/types.ts` — SubstrateModule interface

**Intentionally P4:** This is something Purrsephone should be able to build for herself once the REPL is live. The framework provides the hook points (Lifecycle, registerTool, EventBus.on); she writes the module system.

**Events to add:** module.install, module.uninstall, module.error, module.health

**Depends on:** RLM+REPL epic (modules are self-installed via REPL).
